title: Runtime feature lifecycle and sunset playbook
author: Anika Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines the end-to-end lifecycle for runtime features, kernel variants, and API behaviors at Redwood Inference. It covers how features are proposed, prototyped, benchmarked, instrumented, staged for rollout, monitored during canaries, and eventually deprecated (sunset). The goal is consistent, SLO-aware rollouts that minimize customer impact and preserve reproducible performance baselines.

Scope:
- Applies to changes that affect the serving runtime, scheduler/policy language, kernel implementations, KV cache behavior, and any runtime-exposed configuration flags.
- Excludes purely client-side SDK changes (see eng-developer-experience) and infra-only capacity changes.

Definitions:
- Feature: any new runtime capability or behavioral change (e.g., continuous batching heuristic, new kernel micro-op).
- Kernel variant: a compiled execution path or quantization profile used by the runtime.
- Canary: a controlled rollout to a subset of traffic/instances.
- Sunset: formal deprecation and removal of a feature/kernel.

Feature lifecycle stages (high level):
1) Proposal & design
   - Owner creates a short design doc with: motivation, invariants, expected perf/cost impact, compatibility constraints, and rollout strategy.
   - Required fields: feature id (FR-YYYY-#####), target release, owner, fast rollback plan.
2) Prototype & microbench
   - Implement prototype behind an experimental flag.
   - Run microbench suite (see "Benchmarking" section). Document delta vs baseline for latency P50/P95/P99 and per-token cost.
3) Telemetry & tracing contracts
   - Add kernel/feature labels to traces (tag: runtime.feature_id) and metrics (metric: runtime.feature.{id}.activation_count).
   - Ensure trace spans have consistent start/end semantics for latency attribution.
4) Integration tests & staging
   - Pass unit + integration test matrix including KV cache consistency tests and multi-tenant fairness tests.
   - Run staged workload replay in staging fleet for 48–72 hours.
5) Canary rollout
   - Canary to 1% of traffic or 5 nodes (whichever is larger) for 24 hours; then 5% for 24 hours; then 25% for 48 hours before global.
   - Canary SLO gates: latency P95 < baseline + 15%, error rate delta < 0.05% absolute, token-cost delta < +7%.
6) Global rollout
   - Gradual ramp with automated rollback on gate violation.
7) Stabilization & measurement
   - Run full cost/quality regressions for 14 days and update model performance dashboards.
8) Deprecation / Sunset
   - Publish sunset announcement 90 days before removal for non-security features; 30 days for security patches.

Kernel-specific rollout checklist (must be attached to PR):
- Build artifact naming: kernel.{arch}.{quant}.{tag}. Example: kernel.ampere.q4_0.experimental-v2
- Microbench results: table of sequence lengths [8,64,256,1024] with P50/P95/P99 latency and tokens/sec.
- Quantization validation: decode/re-encode correctness tests and representative generation evals (BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-similarity).
- Memory & eviction tests: confirm kv-cache warmup latency < 200ms for hot sessions.
- Fallback path: define which kernel variant is compatible for automatic fallback; add mapping in scheduler config.

Profiling & benchmarking steps for feature verification:
1) Repro harness: use the operational-workload-simulator (OWS) with recorded production shapes.
2) Microbench protocol:
   - Warm GPU for 30s, run 1000 inferences, record 95th and 99th percentile latencies; repeat 3 times.
   - Use fixed seeds where applicable; publish raw traces to profiling bucket: s3://redwood-runtime-profiling/{feature_id}/{date}/
3) Telemetry correlation:
   - Correlate kernel timings with scheduler events using trace id. Verify no hidden tail spikes introduced by new kernel.
4) Cost test:
   - Run throughput scaling test at 10%, 50%, 100% of expected production concurrency. Capture per-token energy/cost.

Benchmark result reporting template (table):
| metric | baseline | candidate | delta | pass/fail | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P50 latency (seq64) | 12.3ms | 11.7ms | -4.9% | PASS | lower median latency |
| P95 latency (seq64) | 28.9ms | 36.4ms | +26% | FAIL | investigate kernel scheduling interactions |
| tokens/sec (batching 128) | 480 | 532 | +10.8% | PASS | improves throughput |

Release notes and documentation requirements (PR checklist):
- Summary line (one sentence).
- Migration notes for customers (config flags, behavior changes).
- SLO impact statement and measured deltas.
- Known incompatibilities and fallback mappings.
- Tiering: mark feature as "Beta", "GA", or "Experimental".

Runbook: failed canary / rapid rollback procedure (fast path):
1) Canary gate violated: on-call (runtime-oncall@redwood) calls the feature owner and SRE lead within 10 minutes.
2) Immediate action: flip rollout flag to previous kernel (CLI):
```
redwood-runtime rollout apply --feature-id FR-2026-01234 --target previous
```
3) Initiate automated rollback verification: run smoke requests against canary nodes and confirm latency and error rates return to baseline within 10 minutes.
4) Post-incident actions: create postmortem within 72 hours, include traces and experiment artifacts.

Known-issues triage matrix (priority mapping):
- P0: data loss, QoS below SLO for >5 minutes, customer-facing correctness regression. Immediate rollback and all-hands page.
- P1: sustained latency regression P95 > baseline + 30% for >30 minutes. Canary rollback recommended.
- P2: localized performance regression with clear mitigation (config toggle).

Ownership & escalation:
- Feature owner: responsible for design doc, tests, and monitoring during canary.
- Runtime SRE: responsible for rollout automation, metrics alerts, and emergency rollback.
- Release manager: signs off on GA and public release notes.
- Security/Compliance: sign-off required for changes touching key management or telemetry payloads.

Templates & snippets (appendix):
- Feature design header (YAML):
```yaml
feature_id: FR-2026-01234
name: adaptive-batching-heuristic-v2
owner: anika.patel@redwood.ai
target_release: 2026.11
rollout_strategy:
  canary_steps: [1,5,25,100]
  health_gates:
    p95_latency_delta_pct: 15
    error_rate_delta_abs: 0.0005
```
- Canary verification quick queries (metrics):
  - p95_latency_by_model: sum(rate(runtime.latency.p95[5m]))
  - error_rate_total: sum(rate(runtime.errors[5m]))
  - feature_activation: sum(rate(runtime.feature.{id}.activation_count[5m]))

Communication & customer impact:
- For non-breaking changes: post a short announcement in #product-updates and send customer-facing note to accounts with Dedicated/Private deployments when rollout begins.
- For breaking or opt-in changes: open a Customer Advisory (template provided in customer-success-and-support/integration-guides) 30 days prior.

Audit & deprecation timeline (sunset process):
1) Deprecation proposal: owner files a Deprecation Notice with rationale and migration alternatives.
2) Publish notice: 90 days public notice for GA features; 30 days for experimental.
3) Monitoring window: owners must provide compatibility telemetry during notice window.
4) Final removal: remove code & tests in a feature-flagged commit then schedule for release; notify linked customers and update docs.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts to attach to PRs:
- Raw microbench traces: profiling-bucket link
- Perf dashboards: per-model perf board URL
- Canary dashboard snapshot: attach image/PNG
